    import React, { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
    import { Animated, Platform, Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, View } from 'react-native';
    import { LinearGradient } from 'expo-linear-gradient';
    import * as Haptics from 'expo-haptics';
    import type { BottomTabBarProps } from 'expo-router/js-tabs';
    import { useReducedMotionPreference } from '@/hooks/useReducedMotionPreference';
    
    type FloatingTabBarProps = BottomTabBarProps & {
      badgeCounts: Record<string, number>;
    };
    type FloatingTabItemProps = {
      route: BottomTabBarProps['state']['routes'][number];
      options: BottomTabBarProps['descriptors'][string]['options'];
      navigation: BottomTabBarProps['navigation'];
      focused: boolean;
      count: number;
      reduceMotion: boolean;
    };
    
    const RED = '#EF4444';
    
    function useTabMotion(focused: boolean, reduceMotion: boolean) {
      const [progress] = useState(() => new Animated.Value(focused ? 1 : 0));
    
      useEffect(() => {
        if (reduceMotion) {
          progress.setValue(focused ? 1 : 0);
          return;
        }
    
        Animated.spring(progress, {
          toValue: focused ? 1 : 0,
          stiffness: 260,
          damping: 18,
          mass: 0.7,
          useNativeDriver: true,
        }).start();
      }, [focused, progress, reduceMotion]);
    
      return {
        scale: progress.interpolate({ inputRange: [0, 1], outputRange: [1, 1.08] }),
        glow: progress.interpolate({ inputRange: [0, 1], outputRange: [0.12, 0.34] }),
      };
    }
    
    function CountBadge({ count, prominent = false }: { count: number; prominent?: boolean }) {
      if (count <= 0) return null;
    
      return (
        <View style={[styles.countBadge, prominent && styles.prominentCountBadge]}>
          <Text allowFontScaling={false} style={styles.countText}>{count > 9 ? '9+' : count}</Text>
        </View>
      );
    }
    
    function FloatingTabItem({ route, options, navigation, focused, count, reduceMotion }: FloatingTabItemProps) {
      const label = options.title ?? route.name;
      const isToday = route.name === 'index';
      const { scale, glow } = useTabMotion(focused, reduceMotion);
      const color = isToday ? '#FFFFFF' : focused ? '#6D3EF4' : '#6B7E96';
      const icon = options.tabBarIcon?.({ focused, color, size: isToday ? 24 : 23 });
      const accessibilityLabel = count > 0
        ? `${label}, ${route.name === 'inbox'
          ? `${count} unread ${count === 1 ? 'conversation' : 'conversations'}`
          : `${count} ${count === 1 ? 'task' : 'tasks'}`}`
        : label;
    
      const onPress = () => {
        const event = navigation.emit({
          type: 'tabPress',
          target: route.key,
          canPreventDefault: true,
        });
    
        if (!focused && !event.defaultPrevented) {
          navigation.navigate(route.name, route.params);
        }
      };
    
      const onLongPress = () => {
        navigation.emit({ type: 'tabLongPress', target: route.key });
      };
    
      const onPressIn = () => {
        if (Platform.OS === 'ios') void Haptics.impactAsync(Haptics.ImpactFeedbackStyle.Light);
      };
    
      if (isToday) {
        return (
          <>
            <View style={styles.centerSpacer} />
            <Pressable
              testID={`tab-button-${route.name}`}
              accessibilityRole="tab"
              accessibilityLabel={accessibilityLabel}
              accessibilityState={{ selected: focused }}
              onPressIn={onPressIn}
              onPress={onPress}
              onLongPress={onLongPress}
              android_ripple={{ color: '#EDE9FE', borderless: true }}
              style={styles.todayButton}
            >
              <Animated.View testID="today-center-glow" style={[styles.todayGlow, { opacity: glow, transform: [{ scale }] }]} />
              <Animated.View testID="today-center-circle" style={[styles.todayCircle, { transform: [{ scale }] }]}>
                <LinearGradient
                  colors={['#6366F1', '#7C3AED', '#8B5CF6']}
                  start={{ x: 0, y: 0 }}
                  end={{ x: 1, y: 1 }}
                  style={styles.todayGradient}
                >
                  {icon}
                </LinearGradient>
                <CountBadge count={count} prominent />
              </Animated.View>
              <Text allowFontScaling numberOfLines={1} style={[styles.todayLabel, focused && styles.activeLabel]}>
                {label}
              </Text>
            </Pressable>
          </>
        );
      }
    
      return (
        <Pressable
          testID={`tab-button-${route.name}`}
          accessibilityRole="tab"
          accessibilityLabel={accessibilityLabel}
          accessibilityState={{ selected: focused }}
          onPressIn={onPressIn}
          onPress={onPress}
          onLongPress={onLongPress}
          android_ripple={{ color: '#EDE9FE', borderless: true }}
          style={styles.tabButton}
        >
          <Animated.View style={{ transform: [{ scale }] }}>
            {icon}
            <CountBadge count={count} />
          </Animated.View>
          <Text allowFontScaling numberOfLines={1} style={[styles.tabLabel, focused && styles.activeLabel]}>
            {label}
          </Text>
        </Pressable>
      );
    }
    
    export function FloatingTabBar({ state, descriptors, navigation, insets, badgeCounts }: FloatingTabBarProps) {
      const reduceMotion = useReducedMotionPreference();
      const bottomInset = Math.max(0, insets.bottom);
    
      return (
        <View testID="floating-tabbar-background" style={[styles.root, { height: 100 + bottomInset }]}>
          <View style={[
            styles.bar,
            { bottom: bottomInset + 8 },
          ]}>
            {state.routes.map((route, index) => (
              <FloatingTabItem
                key={route.key}
                route={route}
                options={descriptors[route.key].options}
                navigation={navigation}
                focused={state.index === index}
                count={badgeCounts[route.name] ?? 0}
                reduceMotion={reduceMotion}
              />
            ))}
          </View>
        </View>
      );
    }
    
    const styles = StyleSheet.create({
      root: {
        width: '100%',
        overflow: 'visible',
        justifyContent: 'flex-end',
        backgroundColor: 'transparent',
      },
      bar: {
        position: 'absolute',
        left: 18,
        right: 18,
        maxWidth: 520,
        height: 84,
        alignSelf: 'center',
        flexDirection: 'row',
        alignItems: 'center',
        backgroundColor: '#FFFFFF',

        elevation: 10,
        overflow: 'visible',
      },
      tabButton: {
        flex: 1,
        minWidth: 44,
        height: 64,

        justifyContent: 'center',
        gap: 5,
        paddingHorizontal: 2,
      },
      tabLabel: {
        maxWidth: '100%',
        color: '#66778E',
        fontSize: 12,
        fontWeight: '600',
        textAlign: 'center',
      },
      activeLabel: {
        color: '#6D3EF4',
        fontWeight: '800',
      },
      centerSpacer: {
        flex: 1,
        height: 64,
      },
      todayButton: {
        position: 'absolute',
        top: -22,
        left: '50%',
        marginLeft: -37,
        width: 74,
        height: 102,
        alignItems: 'center',
        zIndex: 5,
      },

    import React from 'react';
    import { fireEvent, render } from '@testing-library/react-native';
    import type { BottomTabBarProps } from 'expo-router/js-tabs';
    import { FloatingTabBar } from '../FloatingTabBar';
    
    jest.mock('expo-linear-gradient', () => {
      const ReactModule = require('react');
      const { View } = require('react-native');
      return {
        LinearGradient: ({ children, ...props }: React.PropsWithChildren<Record<string, unknown>>) =>
          ReactModule.createElement(View, props, children),
      };
    });
    jest.mock('expo-haptics', () => ({
      impactAsync: jest.fn(),
      ImpactFeedbackStyle: { Light: 'light' },
    }));
    jest.mock('@/hooks/useReducedMotionPreference', () => ({ useReducedMotionPreference: () => true }));
    
    const routeNames = ['overdue', 'tomorrow', 'index', 'inbox', 'history'];
    const routeLabels = ['Overdue', 'Upcoming', 'Today', 'Inbox', 'History'];
    
    const createProps = (focusedIndex = 2, bottomInset = 0): BottomTabBarProps => {
      const routes = routeNames.map(name => ({ key: `${name}-key`, name, params: undefined }));
      const descriptors = Object.fromEntries(routes.map((route, index) => [route.key, {
        navigation: {},
        route,
        options: {
          title: routeLabels[index],
          tabBarIcon: () => <React.Fragment />,
        },
        render: () => <React.Fragment />,
      }]));
    
      return {
        state: {
          key: 'tabs',
          index: focusedIndex,
          routeNames,
          routes,
          type: 'tab',
          stale: false,
          history: [],
        },
        descriptors,
        navigation: {
          emit: jest.fn(() => ({ defaultPrevented: false })),
          navigate: jest.fn(),
        },
        insets: { top: 0, right: 0, bottom: bottomInset, left: 0 },
      } as unknown as BottomTabBarProps;
    };
    
    describe('FloatingTabBar', () => {
      it('renders the five destinations with Today in the center', () => {
        const { getAllByRole } = render(
          <FloatingTabBar {...createProps()} badgeCounts={{ overdue: 2, tomorrow: 4, index: 1, inbox: 3, history: 0 }} />
        );
    
        expect(getAllByRole('tab').map(tab => tab.props.accessibilityLabel)).toEqual([
          'Overdue, 2 tasks',
          'Upcoming, 4 tasks',
          'Today, 1 task',
          'Inbox, 3 unread conversations',
          'History',
        ]);
      });
    
      it('anchors the prominent Today button to the exact center of the bar', () => {
        const { getByTestId } = render(
          <FloatingTabBar {...createProps()} badgeCounts={{ overdue: 0, tomorrow: 0, index: 0, inbox: 0, history: 0 }} />
        );
    
        expect(getByTestId('tab-button-index')).toHaveStyle({ position: 'absolute', left: '50%' });
      });
    
      it('keeps the Today circle prominent without overpowering the neighboring icons', () => {
        const { getByTestId } = render(
          <FloatingTabBar {...createProps()} badgeCounts={{ overdue: 0, tomorrow: 0, index: 0, inbox: 0, history: 0 }} />
        );
    
        expect(getByTestId('today-center-circle')).toHaveStyle({ width: 60, height: 60 });
        expect(getByTestId('today-center-glow')).toHaveStyle({ width: 66, height: 66 });
      });
    
      it('leaves the shared hills-and-road backdrop visible behind the bar on every tab', () => {
        for (const focusedIndex of [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]) {
          const { getByTestId, unmount } = render(
            <FloatingTabBar {...createProps(focusedIndex)} badgeCounts={{ overdue: 0, tomorrow: 0, index: 0, inbox: 0, history: 0 }} />
          );
    
          expect(getByTestId('floating-tabbar-background')).toHaveStyle({ backgroundColor: 'transparent' });
          unmount();
        }
      });
    
      it('keeps the Today backdrop outside the floating navigation layer', () => {
        const today = render(
          <FloatingTabBar {...createProps(2, 34)} badgeCounts={{ overdue: 0, tomorrow: 0, index: 0, inbox: 0, history: 0 }} />
        );
        expect(today.queryByTestId('tabbar-road-art')).toBeNull();
    
        today.unmount();
        const upcoming = render(
          <FloatingTabBar {...createProps(1)} badgeCounts={{ overdue: 0, tomorrow: 0, index: 0, inbox: 0, history: 0 }} />
        );
        expect(upcoming.queryByTestId('tabbar-road-art')).toBeNull();
      });
    
      it('caps large badge counts at 9+', () => {
        const { getByText } = render(
          <FloatingTabBar {...createProps()} badgeCounts={{ overdue: 12, tomorrow: 0, index: 0, inbox: 0, history: 0 }} />
        );
    
        expect(getByText('9+')).toBeTruthy();
      });
    
      it('emits tabPress and navigates to an unfocused destination', () => {
        const props = createProps(0);
        const { getByTestId } = render(
          <FloatingTabBar {...props} badgeCounts={{ overdue: 0, tomorrow: 0, index: 0, inbox: 0, history: 0 }} />
        );
    
        fireEvent.press(getByTestId('tab-button-tomorrow'));
    
        expect(props.navigation.emit).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
          type: 'tabPress',
          target: 'tomorrow-key',
          canPreventDefault: true,
        });
        expect(props.navigation.navigate).toHaveBeenCalledWith('tomorrow', undefined);
      });
    });

    import React, { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
    import { Animated, Platform, Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, View } from 'react-native';
    import { LinearGradient } from 'expo-linear-gradient';
    import * as Haptics from 'expo-haptics';
    import type { BottomTabBarProps } from 'expo-router/js-tabs';
    import { useReducedMotionPreference } from '@/hooks/useReducedMotionPreference';
    
    type FloatingTabBarProps = BottomTabBarProps & {
      badgeCounts: Record<string, number>;
    };
    type FloatingTabItemProps = {
      route: BottomTabBarProps['state']['routes'][number];
      options: BottomTabBarProps['descriptors'][string]['options'];
      navigation: BottomTabBarProps['navigation'];
      focused: boolean;
      count: number;
      reduceMotion: boolean;
    };
    
    const RED = '#EF4444';
    
    function useTabMotion(focused: boolean, reduceMotion: boolean) {
      const [progress] = useState(() => new Animated.Value(focused ? 1 : 0));
    
      useEffect(() => {
        if (reduceMotion) {
          progress.setValue(focused ? 1 : 0);
          return;
        }
    
        Animated.spring(progress, {
          toValue: focused ? 1 : 0,
          stiffness: 260,
          damping: 18,
          mass: 0.7,
          useNativeDriver: true,
        }).start();
      }, [focused, progress, reduceMotion]);
    
      return {
        scale: progress.interpolate({ inputRange: [0, 1], outputRange: [1, 1.08] }),
        glow: progress.interpolate({ inputRange: [0, 1], outputRange: [0.12, 0.34] }),
      };
    }
    
    function CountBadge({ count, prominent = false }: { count: number; prominent?: boolean }) {
      if (count <= 0) return null;
    
      return (
        <View style={[styles.countBadge, prominent && styles.prominentCountBadge]}>
          <Text allowFontScaling={false} style={styles.countText}>{count > 9 ? '9+' : count}</Text>
        </View>
      );
    }
    
    function FloatingTabItem({ route, options, navigation, focused, count, reduceMotion }: FloatingTabItemProps) {
      const label = options.title ?? route.name;
      const isToday = route.name === 'index';
      const { scale, glow } = useTabMotion(focused, reduceMotion);
      const color = isToday ? '#FFFFFF' : focused ? '#6D3EF4' : '#6B7E96';
      const icon = options.tabBarIcon?.({ focused, color, size: isToday ? 24 : 23 });
      const accessibilityLabel = count > 0
        ? `${label}, ${route.name === 'inbox'
          ? `${count} unread ${count === 1 ? 'conversation' : 'conversations'}`
          : `${count} ${count === 1 ? 'task' : 'tasks'}`}`
        : label;
    
      const onPress = () => {
        const event = navigation.emit({
          type: 'tabPress',
          target: route.key,
          canPreventDefault: true,
        });
    
        if (!focused && !event.defaultPrevented) {
          navigation.navigate(route.name, route.params);
        }
      };
    
      const onLongPress = () => {
        navigation.emit({ type: 'tabLongPress', target: route.key });
      };
    
      const onPressIn = () => {
        if (Platform.OS === 'ios') void Haptics.impactAsync(Haptics.ImpactFeedbackStyle.Light);
      };
    
      if (isToday) {
        return (
          <>
            <View style={styles.centerSpacer} />
            <Pressable
              testID={`tab-button-${route.name}`}
              accessibilityRole="tab"
              accessibilityLabel={accessibilityLabel}
              accessibilityState={{ selected: focused }}
              onPressIn={onPressIn}
              onPress={onPress}
              onLongPress={onLongPress}
              android_ripple={{ color: '#EDE9FE', borderless: true }}
              style={styles.todayButton}
            >
              <Animated.View testID="today-center-glow" style={[styles.todayGlow, { opacity: glow, transform: [{ scale }] }]} />
              <Animated.View testID="today-center-circle" style={[styles.todayCircle, { transform: [{ scale }] }]}>
                <LinearGradient
                  colors={['#6366F1', '#7C3AED', '#8B5CF6']}
                  start={{ x: 0, y: 0 }}
                  end={{ x: 1, y: 1 }}
                  style={styles.todayGradient}
                >
                  {icon}
                </LinearGradient>
                <CountBadge count={count} prominent />
              </Animated.View>
              <Text allowFontScaling numberOfLines={1} style={[styles.todayLabel, focused && styles.activeLabel]}>
                {label}
              </Text>
            </Pressable>
          </>
        );
      }
    
      return (
        <Pressable
          testID={`tab-button-${route.name}`}
          accessibilityRole="tab"
          accessibilityLabel={accessibilityLabel}
          accessibilityState={{ selected: focused }}
          onPressIn={onPressIn}
          onPress={onPress}
          onLongPress={onLongPress}
          android_ripple={{ color: '#EDE9FE', borderless: true }}
          style={styles.tabButton}
        >
          <Animated.View style={{ transform: [{ scale }] }}>
            {icon}
            <CountBadge count={count} />
          </Animated.View>
          <Text allowFontScaling numberOfLines={1} style={[styles.tabLabel, focused && styles.activeLabel]}>
            {label}
          </Text>
        </Pressable>
      );
    }
    
    export function FloatingTabBar({ state, descriptors, navigation, insets, badgeCounts }: FloatingTabBarProps) {
      const reduceMotion = useReducedMotionPreference();
      const bottomInset = Math.max(0, insets.bottom);
    
      return (
        <View testID="floating-tabbar-background" style={[styles.root, { height: 100 + bottomInset }]}>
          <View style={[
            styles.bar,
            { bottom: bottomInset + 8 },
          ]}>
            {state.routes.map((route, index) => (
              <FloatingTabItem
                key={route.key}
                route={route}
                options={descriptors[route.key].options}
                navigation={navigation}
                focused={state.index === index}
                count={badgeCounts[route.name] ?? 0}
                reduceMotion={reduceMotion}
              />
            ))}
          </View>
        </View>
      );
    }
    
    const styles = StyleSheet.create({
      root: {
        width: '100%',
        overflow: 'visible',
        justifyContent: 'flex-end',
        backgroundColor: 'transparent',
      },
      bar: {

## Activity

## Assistant

Yes, **Firebase can store profile pictures**, using **Cloud Storage for Firebase** for the image file. Your app’s database (or Firebase Auth profile) then stores a reference or URL to that file—not the image itself. [Firebase Storage](https://firebase.google.com/docs/storage/) [Firebase Auth user profiles](https://firebase.google.com/docs/auth/admin/manage-users)

A common production flow is: resize/compress the image on the phone, upload it to a user-specific path such as `profile-photos/{userId}/avatar.jpg`, secure uploads with authentication and file type/size rules, then save the image reference to the user record. Firebase Storage supports upload and download security rules. [Storage security rules](https://firebase.google.com/docs/storage/security)

Whether that’s the right choice for this app depends on its existing backend and storage setup.

## Assistant

For this app, the Firebase Android config already points to project **`cfa-rss`** and names a Storage bucket: **`cfa-rss.firebasestorage.app`**. But I found no profile-photo upload code, so the app isn’t currently uploading profile pictures there. The config file alone doesn’t confirm that the bucket is provisioned or accessible.

To set it up in Firebase Console:

1. Open **`cfa-rss` → Databases & Storage → Storage** and create the default bucket if it isn’t already there. Choose a region close to your users; bucket location is hard to change later. Firebase currently requires the **Blaze pay-as-you-go plan** for Cloud Storage, so link billing and set budget alerts first. [Firebase Storage setup and pricing requirements](https://firebase.google.com/docs/storage/web/start) [Firebase billing changes](https://firebase.google.com/docs/storage/faqs-storage-changes-announced-sept-2024)
2. Set **Storage Rules** to require authentication, allow users to upload only to their own profile-photo path, and restrict file size and MIME type to images. Don’t leave production storage publicly writable. [Storage security rules](https://firebase.google.com/docs/storage/security)
3. Enable **App Check** before launch to help ensure requests come from your app. [Firebase Storage setup](https://firebase.google.com/docs/storage/web/start)

The app also needs implementation work: add the Firebase Storage SDK and upload flow, then save the resulting image reference in the app’s existing user profile data. The console configuration by itself won’t add profile-picture functionality.

That message means Cloud Storage is blocked until project `cfa-rss` is on Firebase’s **Blaze pay-as-you-go plan**. Firebase’s current requirement applies even when using the default Storage bucket. [Firebase pricing requirements](https://firebase.google.com/docs/storage/faqs-storage-changes-announced-sept-2024)

To continue, someone with **Owner** access needs to link a Google Cloud Billing account and upgrade the project in Firebase Console. Set a budget alert during setup. Blaze is pay-as-you-go, so check Storage pricing and expected usage before enabling uploads.

After the upgrade, create or open the Storage bucket and configure its access rules. The mobile app will still need code for selecting, uploading, and displaying profile pictures.

Yes, there are alternatives. **Aiven itself is probably not the right place for profile pictures**: the Aiven storage references I found describe storage for service backups and Kafka/ClickHouse tiered data, not a general purpose bucket for app uploads. [Aiven tiered storage](https://aiven.io/docs/products/kafka/concepts/kafka-tiered-storage) [Aiven backup storage](https://aiven.io/docs/platform/concepts/cloud-security)

For this app, I’d consider **Cloudflare R2**. It has a monthly free allowance for standard storage and requests, and it doesn’t charge for internet egress. Above those allowances, usage is billed. [R2 pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/pricing/)

The app’s backend can authorize each upload and save the resulting object key or URL in its existing user database. That keeps storage credentials out of the mobile app. Your project config currently names a Firebase Storage bucket, but I found no profile-photo upload implementation.

One caveat: R2 still requires configuring the bucket, access controls, and billing with Cloudflare. Aiven can remain your database provider while R2 stores the image files.

## Assistant

Yes. **Filestack offers a free plan with no credit card required:** 1 GB storage, 1 GB monthly bandwidth, and 500 uploads through its API or file picker. That could work for a small profile-picture feature, but you’d need to check whether its limits and terms fit your expected use. [Filestack free plan](https://go.filestack.com/signup-free/)

For production, keep its API credentials on your backend and have the app upload through your server. Don’t put a secret key directly in the mobile app. Also, the uploaded pictures would be hosted by Filestack, while your existing database stores each user’s image URL.

One tradeoff: it’s a third-party service with limited free quotas; exceeding them may require payment.

## Assistant

This spans three product surfaces plus login/profile persistence, so I’m treating it as an architectural design rather than a small header tweak. I found the rider app currently logs in by email then PIN, while web admin reads rider names from API responses and SQL; I’m checking those shared contracts and screens to keep the avatar source consistent.

    const loginHero = require('../assets/images/login-hero-rider.png');

    const loginSurfaceColor = '#F8FAFC';
    
    const statusConfig = {

      ready: { color: '#22C55E', label: 'System Ready' },
      offline: { color: '#EF4444', label: 'Server Offline' },
    } as const;
    
    export default function LoginScreen() {
      const { login } = useAuth();
      const { width, height } = useWindowDimensions();

      const heroImageWidth = heroHeight * (2048 / 684);
    
      // State
      const [step, setStep] = useState<'email' | 'pin'>('email');
      const [email, setEmail] = useState('');
      const [password, setPassword] = useState('');
      const [keepSignedIn, setKeepSignedIn] = useState(false);
      const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);

      const transition = useSharedValue(0);

      // PIN Translation Mapping
      const translatePinToPassword = (pin: string) => {
        const PIN_MAP: Record<string, string> = {
          '0001': 'rider1',
          '0002': 'rider2',
          '1234': 'rider1',
        };
        return PIN_MAP[pin] || pin;

        }
    
        setError('');
        setLoading(true);
    
        const finalPassword = translatePinToPassword(password);

            </View>

              testID="login_hero_curve"

              <Path
                d="M 0 25 C 80 -5, 135 45, 215 25 C 290 5, 345 5, 400 25 L 400 65 L 0 65 Z"
                fill={loginSurfaceColor}

            </Svg>
          </View>
    
          <ImageBackground
            testID="login_footer_image"

              <ActivityIndicator color="#702CF6" size="large" style={styles.loadingIndicator} />

                    </View>
    
                    <View style={styles.stepsWrapper}>

                        </Animated.View>

                          <View style={styles.pinEntryContainer}>

                                  accessibilityLabel={`PIN digit ${index + 1}`}
                                  style={[
                                    styles.pinSlot,
                                    index === password.length && styles.pinSlotActive,
                                    password.length > index && styles.pinSlotFilled,
                                  ]}
                                >
                                  <Text style={[styles.pinSlotDot, password.length > index && styles.pinSlotDotFilled]}>
                                    {password.length > index ? 'â—' : ''}
                                  </Text>
                                </View>
                              ))}
                            </View>
                            <TextInput
                              testID="login_pin_input"
                              accessibilityLabel="4-digit PIN"
                              accessibilityHint="Enter four digits using the numeric keyboard"
                              accessibilityRole="text"
                              style={styles.pinInputOverlay}
                              value={password}
                              onChangeText={(value) => { setPassword(value.replace(/\D/g, '').slice(0, 4)); setError(''); }}
                              keyboardType="number-pad"
                              secureTextEntry
                              maxLength={4}
                              autoComplete="off"
                              textContentType="oneTimeCode"
                              caretHidden
                              selectionColor="transparent"

                          </View>
    
                          <View testID="login_pin_options_row" style={styles.pinOptionsRow}>
                            <TouchableOpacity
                              testID="login_keep_signed_in_checkbox"

                              accessibilityLabel="Keep me signed in on this device"

                              style={styles.keepSignedInControl}

                            >
                              <View style={[styles.keepSignedInBox, keepSignedIn && styles.keepSignedInBoxChecked]}>
                                {keepSignedIn && <MaterialIcons name="check" size={moderateScale(15)} color="#FFFFFF" />}
                              </View>
                              <Text style={styles.keepSignedInText}>Keep me signed in</Text>
                            </TouchableOpacity>
    
                            <TouchableOpacity
                              testID="login_forgot_pin_button"
                              accessibilityRole="button"
                              style={styles.forgotPinButton}
                              onPress={() => Alert.alert(
                                'Need Assistance?',

                              )}
                              activeOpacity={0.75}
                            >
                              <Text style={styles.forgotPinText}>Forgot your PIN?</Text>
                            </TouchableOpacity>
                          </View>
    
                          <TouchableOpacity
                            testID="login_sign_in_button"
                            accessibilityRole="button"
                            accessibilityState={{ disabled: password.length !== 4 }}
                            disabled={password.length !== 4}
                            style={[styles.primaryButton, password.length !== 4 && styles.buttonDisabled]}
                            onPress={handleLogin}
                            activeOpacity={0.85}
                          >
                            <LinearGradient colors={['#635BFF', '#7C2CF5']} start={{ x: 0, y: 0 }} end={{ x: 1, y: 0 }} style={styles.primaryButtonGradient}>
                              <View style={styles.primaryButtonContent}>
                                <Text style={styles.primaryButtonText}>Sign In</Text>
                                <MaterialIcons name="arrow-forward" size={moderateScale(22)} color="#FFFFFF" />
                              </View>
                            </LinearGradient>
                          </TouchableOpacity>
                        </Animated.View>
                      )}
                    </View>
    
                    <TouchableOpacity
                      testID="login_support_button"
                      accessibilityRole="button"
                      style={styles.supportButton}
                      onPress={() => Alert.alert(
                        'Need Assistance?',
                        'Please contact your dispatch supervisor for PIN/Email verification support.',
                      )}
                      activeOpacity={0.75}
                    >
                      <Text style={styles.supportText}>Help & Support</Text>
                    </TouchableOpacity>
                  </View>
                </View>
              </KeyboardAvoidingView>
            </ScrollView>
          )}
    
          <PasswordResetOverlay
            visible={resetModalVisible}
            userId={resetUserId}
            onClose={() => setResetModalVisible(false)}
            onSuccess={() => {
              setResetModalVisible(false);
              Alert.alert('Success', 'Password updated! Please login with your new credentials.');
              handleBack();
            }}
          />
        </SafeAreaView>
      );
    }

    import React from 'react';

    export default function TabLayout() {
      const colorScheme = useColorScheme();
      const insets = useSafeAreaInsets();
      const { user } = useAuth();
      const { attendanceStatus } = useLocation();
      const { handleLogout } = useDashboard();
      const unreadMessages = useMessagingUnread();
    
      const { data: tasks = [] } = useQuery({
        queryKey: ['tasks', user?.id],
        queryFn: getTasks,
        enabled: !!user?.id,
        refetchInterval: 30000,
      });
    
      const counts = getRiderTaskCounts(tasks);
    
      if (attendanceStatus === 'absent' || attendanceStatus === 'on_leave') {
        return (
          <AttendanceLockout
            status={attendanceStatus as any}
            onLogout={handleLogout}
          />
        );
      }
    
      return (

          <TodayRoadBackdrop />
          <Tabs
            initialRouteName="index"
            tabBar={props => (
              <FloatingTabBar
                {...props}
                badgeCounts={{
                  overdue: counts.overdue,
                  tomorrow: counts.upcoming,
                  index: counts.today,
                  inbox: unreadMessages,
                }}
              />
            )}
            screenOptions={{
              tabBarActiveTintColor: Colors[colorScheme === 'dark' ? 'dark' : 'light'].tint,
              headerShown: false,
              sceneStyle: { backgroundColor: 'transparent' },

                  backgroundColor: 'transparent',
                  borderTopWidth: 0,

                  backgroundColor: 'transparent',
                  borderTopWidth: 0,
                  elevation: 0,
                },
              }),
            }}
          >
            <Tabs.Screen name="overdue" options={{
              title: 'Overdue',
              tabBarIcon: ({ color }) => <Ionicons name="alert-circle-outline" size={23} color={color} />,
            }} />
            <Tabs.Screen name="tomorrow" options={{
              title: 'Upcoming',
              tabBarIcon: ({ color }) => <Ionicons name="calendar-outline" size={23} color={color} />,
            }} />
            <Tabs.Screen name="index" options={{
              title: 'Today',
              tabBarIcon: () => <MaterialCommunityIcons name="calendar-check" size={27} color="#FFFFFF" />,
            }} />
            <Tabs.Screen name="inbox" options={{
              title: 'Inbox',
              tabBarIcon: ({ color }) => <Ionicons name="mail-outline" size={23} color={color} />,
            }} />
            <Tabs.Screen name="history" options={{
              title: 'History',
              tabBarIcon: ({ color }) => <Ionicons name="time-outline" size={23} color={color} />,
            }} />
          </Tabs>
        </View>
      );
    }

              <TouchableOpacity testID="header_logout_button" accessibilityLabel="Log out" onPress={onLogoutPress} style={[styles.iconButton, styles.logoutButton]}>

      );

    import React, { createContext, useState, useContext, useEffect, useMemo } from 'react';
    import AsyncStorage from '@react-native-async-storage/async-storage';
    import { api, setAuthFailureListener, resetAuthStatus } from '@/utils/api';
    import { useRootNavigationState, useRouter, useSegments } from 'expo-router';
    
    import { AuthManager } from '@/utils/AuthManager';
    import { getAuthRedirect } from '@/utils/authNavigation';
    
    type AuthContextType = {
      user: any;
      token: string | null;
      isLoading: boolean;
      login: (email: string, password: string, keepSignedIn: boolean) => Promise<{
        success: boolean;
        requirePasswordReset?: boolean;
        userId?: string;
        error?: string;
      }>;
      logout: () => Promise<void>;
    };
    
    const AuthContext = createContext<AuthContextType | null>(null);
    
    export function useAuth() {
      const context = useContext(AuthContext);
      if (!context) {
        throw new Error('useAuth must be used within an AuthProvider');
      }
      return context;
    }
    
    export function AuthProvider({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
      const [user, setUser] = useState<any>(null);
      const [token, setToken] = useState<string | null>(null);
      const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(true);
      const segments = useSegments();
      const router = useRouter();
      const navigationState = useRootNavigationState();
    
      useEffect(() => {
        const redirect = getAuthRedirect({
          isLoading,
          user,
          firstSegment: segments[0],
          navigationReady: Boolean(navigationState?.key),
        });
        if (redirect) router.replace(redirect);
      }, [user, isLoading, navigationState?.key, router, segments]);
    
      useEffect(() => {
        // Listen for global auth failures (401s)
        setAuthFailureListener(() => {
          console.warn('[AUTH] Global interceptor triggered logout');
          setToken(null);
          setUser(null);
        });
    
        const check = async () => {
          try {
            const shouldRestoreSession = await AuthManager.shouldRestoreSession();
            if (!shouldRestoreSession) {
              await AuthManager.clearSession();
              setToken(null);
              setUser(null);
              return;
            }
    
            const userData = await AuthManager.getUserData();
            const token = await AuthManager.getValidToken();
    
            if (token && userData) {
              resetAuthStatus();
              setToken(token);
              setUser(userData);
            } else {
              await AuthManager.clearSession();
              setToken(null);
              setUser(null);
            }
          } finally {
            setIsLoading(false);
          }
        };
        check();
      }, []);
    
      const login = async (email: string, password: string, keepSignedIn: boolean) => {
        try {
          const res = await api.post('/api/auth/login', { email, password });
          const data = res.data;
    
          // Handle password reset requirement
          if (data.require_password_reset) {
            return {
              success: false,
              requirePasswordReset: true,
              userId: data.id || data.userId
            };
          }
    
          if (data.token && data.refreshToken) {
            await AuthManager.saveSession(data.token, data.refreshToken, data, keepSignedIn);
            resetAuthStatus();
            setToken(data.token);
            setUser(data);
            return { success: true };
          }
          return { success: false, error: 'No token' };
        } catch (err: any) {
          return { success: false, error: err.response?.data?.error || 'Fail' };
        }
      };
    
      const logout = async () => {
        try {
          await api.post('/api/auth/logout', { userId: user?.id });
        } catch (e) {}
        await AuthManager.clearSession();
    
        // --- PRIVACY SYNC: Clear duty status ---
        await AsyncStorage.setItem('@is_on_duty', 'false');
    
        await AsyncStorage.multiRemove(['@rider_id', '@active_request_id']);
        resetAuthStatus();
        setToken(null);
        setUser(null);
      };
    
      const value = useMemo(() => ({ user, token, isLoading, login, logout }), [user, token, isLoading]);
      return <AuthContext.Provider value={value as any}>{children}</AuthContext.Provider>;
    }

    }
    
    export const ScreenHeader: React.FC<ScreenHeaderProps> = ({
      variant = 'default',
      title,
      subtitle,
      badgeLabel,
      badgeStatus = 'info',
      titleAccessory,
      onNotifPress,
      onLogoutPress,
      unreadCount = 0,
    }) => {
      if (variant === 'hero') {
        return (
          <LinearGradient
            colors={['#0B3554', '#17586B', '#397B78']}
            start={{ x: 0, y: 0.5 }}

            testID="hero-header"
            style={styles.heroHeader}
          >
            <View pointerEvents="none" style={styles.heroArtwork}>

              <View testID="hero-title-row" style={styles.heroTitleRow}>
                <Text numberOfLines={1} adjustsFontSizeToFit style={styles.heroTitle}>{title}</Text>
                {titleAccessory}
              </View>
              <View style={styles.actions}>
                <TouchableOpacity
                  testID="header_notifications_button"
                  accessibilityRole="button"
                  accessibilityLabel={unreadCount > 0 ? `Notifications, ${unreadCount} unread` : 'Notifications'}
                  onPress={onNotifPress}
                  style={styles.heroButtonHitArea}
                >
                  <View testID="header_notifications_surface" style={styles.heroButtonSurface}>
                    <MaterialIcons name="notifications-none" size={17} color="#173B56" />
                  </View>
                  {unreadCount > 0 && (
                    <View style={styles.heroNotifBadge}>
                      <Text style={styles.heroNotifBadgeText}>{unreadCount > 9 ? '9+' : unreadCount}</Text>
                    </View>
                  )}
                </TouchableOpacity>
                <TouchableOpacity
                  testID="header_logout_button"
                  accessibilityRole="button"
                  accessibilityLabel="Log out"
                  onPress={onLogoutPress}

                >
                  <View style={[styles.heroButtonSurface, styles.heroLogoutButton]}>
                    <MaterialIcons name="logout" size={16} color="#EF4444" />
                  </View>
                </TouchableOpacity>
              </View>
            </View>
            {subtitle && <Text style={styles.heroSubtitle}>{subtitle}</Text>}

    export class MessagingServiceError extends Error {
      constructor(
        public readonly code: 'NOT_FOUND' | 'FORBIDDEN' | 'CONVERSATION_CLOSED' | 'VALIDATION_ERROR' | 'INVALID_CURSOR',

    let tablesReady: Promise<void> | null = null;
    
    async function ensureMessagingCollation(): Promise<void> {
      const [columns] = await pool.query(`
        SELECT DISTINCT TABLE_NAME
        FROM information_schema.COLUMNS
        WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA = DATABASE()
          AND TABLE_NAME IN (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
          AND COLLATION_NAME IS NOT NULL
          AND COLLATION_NAME <> ?
      `, [...MESSAGING_TABLES, MESSAGING_COLLATION]) as any[];
    
      for (const row of columns as Array<{ TABLE_NAME: string }>) {
        if (!MESSAGING_TABLES.includes(row.TABLE_NAME as typeof MESSAGING_TABLES[number])) continue;
        await pool.query(
          `ALTER TABLE \`${row.TABLE_NAME}\` CONVERT TO CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE ${MESSAGING_COLLATION}`,
        );
      }
    }
    
    export async function ensureMessagingTables(): Promise<void> {
      if (!tablesReady) {
        tablesReady = (async () => {
          await pool.query(`
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS conversations (
              id VARCHAR(191) NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
              request_id VARCHAR(191) NOT NULL,
              rider_id VARCHAR(191) NOT NULL,
              status ENUM('open', 'closed') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open',
              last_message_at TIMESTAMP(6) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(6),
              created_at TIMESTAMP(6) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(6),
              updated_at TIMESTAMP(6) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(6) ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(6),
              UNIQUE KEY uq_conversations_request_rider (request_id, rider_id),
              INDEX idx_conversations_last_message (last_message_at, id),
              INDEX idx_conversations_rider (rider_id, status)
            ) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci
          `);
          await pool.query(`
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS conversation_participants (
              conversation_id VARCHAR(191) NOT NULL,
              user_id VARCHAR(191) NOT NULL,
              last_read_at TIMESTAMP(6) NULL DEFAULT NULL,
              created_at TIMESTAMP(6) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(6),
              UNIQUE KEY uq_conversation_participants (conversation_id, user_id),
              INDEX idx_conversation_participants_user (user_id, conversation_id)
            ) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci
          `);
          await pool.query(`
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS messages (
              id VARCHAR(191) NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
              conversation_id VARCHAR(191) NOT NULL,
              sender_id VARCHAR(191) NOT NULL,
              client_message_id VARCHAR(191) NOT NULL,
              body VARCHAR(4000) NOT NULL,
              created_at TIMESTAMP(6) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(6),
              read_at TIMESTAMP(6) NULL DEFAULT NULL,
              UNIQUE KEY uq_messages_sender_client (sender_id, client_message_id),
              INDEX idx_messages_conversation_cursor (conversation_id, created_at, id),
              INDEX idx_messages_sender_created (sender_id, created_at)
            ) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci
          `);
          await ensureMessagingCollation();
        })().catch((error) => {
          tablesReady = null;
          throw error;
        });
      }
      await tablesReady;
    }
    
    function clampLimit(limit: number | undefined): number {
      if (!Number.isFinite(limit)) return DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE;

    }
    
    function encodeCursor(createdAt: string, id: string): string {
      return Buffer.from(JSON.stringify([createdAt, id])).toString('base64url');
    }
    
    function decodeCursor(cursor: string | null | undefined): [string, string] | null {
      if (!cursor) return null;
      try {
        const decoded = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(cursor, 'base64url').toString('utf8'));
        if (!Array.isArray(decoded) || decoded.length !== 2 || decoded.some((value) => typeof value !== 'string' || !value)) {
          throw new Error('Invalid cursor');
        }
        return [decoded[0], decoded[1]];
      } catch {
        throw new MessagingServiceError('INVALID_CURSOR', 'The pagination cursor is invalid.');
      }
    }

        dr.request_type, dr.delivery_status, dr.pickup_address, dr.dropoff_address,

## Assistant

The cleanest fit appears to be a fixed catalog of bundled avatars, with only a small `avatar_id` saved on the existing Aiven-backed user record. That avoids image hosting and lets both apps render the same selection; I’m checking deployment/schema conventions and the admin surfaces before I recommend the exact flow.

    function useMediaQuery(query: string) {
      const getMatches = () => typeof window !== "undefined" && window.matchMedia(query).matches;
      const [matches, setMatches] = useState(getMatches);
    
      useEffect(() => {
        const mediaQuery = window.matchMedia(query);
        const handleChange = () => setMatches(mediaQuery.matches);
    
        handleChange();
        mediaQuery.addEventListener?.("change", handleChange);
        return () => mediaQuery.removeEventListener?.("change", handleChange);
      }, [query]);
    
      return matches;
    }

    # Rider Avatar Profiles Design
    
    ## Summary
    
    Give riders a small, selectable set of neutral illustrated DiceBear avatars. Store only a stable avatar ID in the existing application user record; do not store uploaded image bytes or depend on Firebase Storage. Render the selected avatar consistently in the rider app and web admin.
    
    ## Goals
    
    - Let an authenticated rider select and change a profile avatar in the mobile app.
    - Persist the choice in the existing Aiven-backed user database so it follows the rider across sessions and devices.
    - Show the same avatar in the mobile login success welcome, Admin Map, Inbox, and Dispatch assignment UI.
    - Keep the existing login and PIN authentication semantics, and show personalized welcome content only after successful authentication.
    - Provide a reliable fallback for users with no selection or an unknown avatar ID.
    
    ## Non-goals
    
    - Uploading personal photos or other user-provided files.
    - Firebase Authentication, Cloud Storage, or other image-hosting setup.
    - Allowing arbitrary DiceBear style/options to be submitted by a client.
    - Reworking unrelated login, header, map, dispatch, or messaging behavior.
    
    ## Approved direction
    
    Generate a curated, fixed catalog of neutral DiceBear avatars and bundle equivalent assets with both apps. The two applications use the same stable IDs and visually identical artwork. Store the selected ID (for example, `avatar_01`) on the rider profile. The catalog is controlled by application code; clients submit only an ID from that catalog. Review and preserve the selected DiceBear style's license and attribution requirements before bundling the generated assets.
    
    The public DiceBear API is not used at runtime. This avoids third-party image requests, runtime availability issues, data leakage through avatar seeds, and broken/offline rendering. Since both applications need to render the same selection and React Native/web SVG support can differ, build-time generated static assets are the cross-platform source of truth.
    
    ## User experience
    
    ### Rider app settings
    
    - Add a clearly labeled Settings action to the existing rider header, with an accessible name and a touch target of at least 44 by 44 points.
    - Settings contains a profile section with the rider's name, current avatar, and a compact grid of curated choices.
    - Each avatar choice is keyboard/accessibility identifiable, exposes selected state, and has a visible selected treatment that does not rely on color alone.
    - Saving updates the signed-in rider's profile through the authenticated backend. Show progress and a clear success or recoverable error state. Keep the previous selection visible if saving fails.
    - The picker works with the bundled assets while offline; the server save can be retried after connectivity returns, but the UI must not claim the choice is saved until the server confirms it.
    
    ### Login success welcome
    
    - Preserve the current splash screen and email-to-PIN login flow.
    - After the backend confirms a successful PIN login, show a brief welcome state with the transparent-background logo, the copy `Welcome Back, Rider [Name]`, and the chosen avatar.
    - The welcome appears only for a fresh successful login, not on app cold start/session restore or failed login attempts.
    - Continue into the normal authenticated landing screen automatically. Respect reduced-motion preferences and avoid making the welcome animation block access for an extended time.
    - If the profile has no known avatar ID, use the app's person/initial fallback.
    
    ## Data contract and persistence
    
    - Add nullable `avatar_id` to the `users` table. Existing accounts remain valid with `NULL` and render the fallback.
    - Add an idempotent database migration following the repository's migration script conventions. Do not store avatar URLs or generated SVG strings in the database.
    - Extend the shared user profile contract to include `avatar_id: string | null`.
    - Include this field in the mobile login/refresh profile payload, authenticated rider profile reads, admin rider lists, and live-rider API responses used by map and dispatch.
    - Add an authenticated self-service endpoint for updating the current user's avatar. It accepts only a catalog ID or `null` (if clearing selection is supported), validates role and input, updates only the caller's own row, and returns the canonical profile field. Riders cannot update another user's avatar.
    - The Inbox conversation summary query returns the rider's `avatar_id`; update server and web messaging types accordingly.
    - Use a single catalog definition or generated catalog artifact with stable IDs, asset mapping, and fallback behavior. Do not accept arbitrary URLs or style names from the client.
    
    ## Web admin presentation
    
    - Admin Map: display the avatar in the rider identity treatment (map marker/card/detail where rider identity is shown); keep existing live status, name, and map interactions intact.
    - Inbox: use the avatar in conversation list and selected conversation header, preserving rider name and online/unread indicators.
    - Dispatch: use the avatar in rider assignment choices and tracking identity surfaces where available, preserving availability, selection, and assignment behavior.
    - All locations use the shared ID-to-asset mapping and fall back to initials/person icon for null, missing, or unknown IDs.
    - Set non-decorative image alternatives to rider name; mark decorative duplicates appropriately for assistive technology.
    
    ## Error handling and compatibility
    
    - Migration is safe to re-run and does not rewrite existing user profile data.
    - An invalid avatar ID receives a validation response and never persists.
    - A failed profile update leaves the currently saved avatar in place and communicates the failure without losing the rest of Settings state.
    - Existing login, refresh, rider listing, map, dispatch, and messaging consumers continue to work when `avatar_id` is null or omitted during gradual rollout.
    - Static assets remain available without network access. If an asset fails to render, use the existing initials/person fallback.
    
    ## Security and privacy
    
    - Avatar updates use existing authenticated session and role middleware.
    - The API derives target user ID from the authenticated principal; no client-supplied target ID is accepted for self-service updates.
    - Do not send email, name, or user ID as a DiceBear seed to a third-party runtime API. Static generated assets contain no per-user personal data.
    - Do not expose authentication secrets or include new personal data in logs.
    
    ## Validation
    
    - Server tests: migration behavior, avatar ID allowlist validation, rider-only self-update, cannot update another user, and profile serialization.
    - Mobile tests: settings opens, catalog selection/selected state, save success/failure, offline asset rendering, login welcome only after successful fresh login, correct rider name/avatar, and no welcome on restored session.
    - Web tests: admin Map, Inbox list/detail, and Dispatch assignment render matching assets and fallbacks for null/unknown IDs without changing existing interactions.
    - Run checks for touched packages in repo quality-gate order: lint, typecheck, test, build. Refresh Graphify after code changes.
    
    ## Rollout
    
    1. Add the nullable schema column and backend compatibility fields first.
    2. Bundle the same catalog in mobile and web, and update admin surfaces to handle null values.
    3. Add the mobile avatar selector and persist the profile choice.
    4. Add the fresh-login welcome state.
    5. Verify a selected avatar flows from a rider's profile into all three admin surfaces.
    
    ## Design review notes
    
    - The avatar set must be small and visually coherent; final count and exact licensed DiceBear style are implementation choices within this design.
    - The current app login is a single screen with email followed by PIN. The new welcome is a transient post-auth state and must integrate with existing auth redirects without appearing during restored sessions.
    - The existing `ScreenHeader` includes notifications and logout; add Settings without removing or crowding those controls. Preserve accessible target sizing on narrow mobile screens.

    # Writing Plans
    
    ## Overview
    
    Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.
    
    Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.
    
    **Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."
    
    **Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.
    
    **Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
    - (User preferences for plan location override this default)
    
    ## Scope Check
    
    If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans â€” one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.
    
    ## File Structure
    
    Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.
    
    - Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
    - You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
    - Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
    - In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.
    
    This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.
    
    ## Task Right-Sizing
    
    A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
    fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
    configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
    deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
    reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
    independently testable deliverable.
    
    ## Bite-Sized Task Granularity
    
    **Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
    - "Write the failing test" - step
    - "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
    - "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
    - "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
    - "Commit" - step
    
    ## Plan Document Header
    
    **Every plan MUST start with this header:**
    
    ```markdown
    # [Feature Name] Implementation Plan
    
    > **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
    
    **Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]
    
    **Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]
    
    **Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]
    
    **Spec:** [path to the spec/design doc this plan implements â€” the plan
    argues from the spec, so the spec travels with it; executors read both]
    
    ## Global Constraints
    
    [The spec's project-wide requirements â€” version floors, dependency limits,
    naming and copy rules, platform requirements â€” one line each, with exact
    values copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly
    include this section.]
    
    ## Review Focus
    
    [The five input classes or failure modes the spec implies but no task's
    tests exercise that are most likely to bite a person using this software
    â€” one line each, naming the input or condition and the behavior a
    reasonable person would expect, most likely first. The spec is a vision
    document: it says what the software must do, not everything it will
    meet, and its silence on an input is not permission for that input to
    break the program. Write the list here, once, with the spec in front of
    you. Then, for each line, add the test that pins it to the task that
    owns the code, in that task's own step style.]
    
    ---
    ```
    
    ## Task Structure
    
    ````markdown
    ### Task N: [Component Name]
    
    **Files:**
    - Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
    - Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
    - Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`
    
    **Interfaces:**
    - Consumes: [what this task uses from earlier tasks â€” exact signatures]
    - Produces: [what later tasks rely on â€” exact function names, parameter
      and return types. A task's implementer sees only their own task; this
      block is how they learn the names and types neighboring tasks use.]
    
    - [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**
    
    ```python
    def test_specific_behavior():
        result = function(input)
        assert result == expected
    ```
    
    - [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**
    
    Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
    Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"
    
    - [ ] **Step 3: Write minimal implementation**
    
    ```python
    def function(input):
        return expected
    ```
    
    - [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**
    
    Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
    Expected: PASS
    
    - [ ] **Step 5: Commit**
    
    ```bash
    git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
    git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
    ```
    ````
    
    ## No Placeholders
    
    Every step must contain the actual content an engineer needs. These are **plan failures** â€” never write them:
    - "TBD", "TODO", "implement later", "fill in details"
    - "Add appropriate error handling" / "add validation" / "handle edge cases"
    - "Write tests for the above" (without actual test code)
    - "Similar to Task N" (repeat the code â€” the engineer may be reading tasks out of order)
    - Steps that describe what to do without showing how (code blocks required for code steps)
    - References to types, functions, or methods not defined in any task
    
    ## Self-Review
    
    After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself â€” not a subagent dispatch.
    
    **1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.
    
    **2. Placeholder scan:** Search your plan for red flags â€” any of the patterns from the "No Placeholders" section above. Fix them.
    
    **3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.
    
    **4. Review Focus:** For each input class or failure mode the spec implies, is there a task whose tests exercise it? The five uncovered ones most likely to bite a person go in the Review Focus section, and each line there gets its test added to the owning task. An empty section means you checked and found none, not that you skipped the check.
    
    If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review â€” just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.
    
    ## Execution Handoff
    
    After saving and self-reviewing the plan, link it for your human partner
    to read. If they have already explicitly supplied an execution method, ask
    them to review the plan and confirm it captures what they want; wait for that
    review before implementation, then use the preserved method. Otherwise, ask
    them to review the plan and choose an execution method before implementation.
    
    **When no execution method has already been supplied:**
    
    **"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Please review the plan. Which execution approach would you prefer?**
    
    - **Subagent-driven** - A fresh subagent implements each task and a fresh reviewer checks it before the next one starts, then a whole-branch review at the end. Most thorough; costs a fresh context per task and per review.
    - **Native** - I implement every task myself in this session, the way this harness runs work, then one fresh reviewer on the most capable model checks the whole branch. Cheapest and fastest; no independent review until the end. Runs well with a mid-tier session model, since the plan carries the design.
    
    **For this plan I recommend <one of the two>, because <one sentence from the plan: how much the tasks depend on each other's interfaces, how many there are, what a shipped mistake would cost>. Does the plan capture what you want, and which approach should we use?"**
    
    **When an execution method has already been supplied:**
    
    **"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Please review the plan. Does it capture what you want?"**

    - **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development

    # Rider Avatar Profiles Design
    
    ## Summary
    
    Give riders a small, selectable set of neutral illustrated DiceBear avatars. Store only a stable avatar ID in the existing application user record; do not store uploaded image bytes or depend on Firebase Storage. Render the selected avatar consistently in the rider app and web admin.
    
    ## Goals
    
    - Let an authenticated rider select and change a profile avatar in the mobile app.
    - Persist the choice in the existing Aiven-backed user database so it follows the rider across sessions and devices.
    - Show the same avatar in the mobile login success welcome, Admin Map, Inbox, and Dispatch assignment UI.
    - Keep the existing login and PIN authentication semantics, and show personalized welcome content only after successful authentication.
    - Provide a reliable fallback for users with no selection or an unknown avatar ID.
    
    ## Non-goals
    
    - Uploading personal photos or other user-provided files.
    - Firebase Authentication, Cloud Storage, or other image-hosting setup.
    - Allowing arbitrary DiceBear style/options to be submitted by a client.
    - Reworking unrelated login, header, map, dispatch, or messaging behavior.
    
    ## Approved direction
    
    Generate a curated catalog of eight neutral DiceBear avatars using the `lorelei-neutral` style and bundle equivalent static PNG assets with both apps. DiceBear lists this style under CC0 1.0. Preserve the style license/source notice with the assets. The two applications use the same stable IDs (`avatar_01` through `avatar_08`) and visually identical artwork. Store the selected ID on the rider profile. The catalog is controlled by application code; clients submit only an ID from that catalog.
    
    The public DiceBear API is not used at runtime. This avoids third-party image requests, runtime availability issues, data leakage through avatar seeds, and broken/offline rendering. Since both applications need to render the same selection and React Native/web SVG support can differ, build-time generated static assets are the cross-platform source of truth.
    
    ## User experience
    
    ### Rider app settings
    
    - Add a clearly labeled Settings action to the existing rider header, with an accessible name and a touch target of at least 44 by 44 points.
    - Settings contains a profile section with the rider's name, current avatar, and a compact grid of curated choices.
    - Each avatar choice is keyboard/accessibility identifiable, exposes selected state, and has a visible selected treatment that does not rely on color alone.
    - Saving updates the signed-in rider's profile through the authenticated backend. Show progress and a clear success or recoverable error state. Keep the previous selection visible if saving fails.
    - The picker works with the bundled assets while offline; the server save can be retried after connectivity returns, but the UI must not claim the choice is saved until the server confirms it.
    
    ### Login success welcome
    
    - Preserve the current splash screen and email-to-PIN login flow.
    - After the backend confirms a successful PIN login, show a brief welcome state with the transparent-background logo, the copy `Welcome Back, Rider [Name]`, and the chosen avatar.
    - The welcome appears only for a fresh successful login, not on app cold start/session restore or failed login attempts.
    - Continue into the normal authenticated landing screen automatically. Respect reduced-motion preferences and avoid making the welcome animation block access for an extended time.
    - If the profile has no known avatar ID, use the app's person/initial fallback.
    
    ## Data contract and persistence
    
    - Add nullable `avatar_id` to the `users` table. Existing accounts remain valid with `NULL` and render the fallback.
    - Add an idempotent database migration following the repository's migration script conventions. Do not store avatar URLs or generated SVG strings in the database.
    - Extend the shared user profile contract to include `avatar_id: string | null`.
    - Include this field in the mobile login/refresh profile payload, authenticated rider profile reads, admin rider lists, and live-rider API responses used by map and dispatch.
    - Add an authenticated self-service endpoint for updating the current user's avatar. It accepts only one of the eight catalog IDs, validates that the caller is a rider, updates only the caller's own row, and returns the canonical profile field. The first version does not include a clear-avatar action; existing null values remain supported as legacy profiles.
    - The Inbox conversation summary query returns the rider's `avatar_id`; update server and web messaging types accordingly.
    - Use a single catalog definition or generated catalog artifact with stable IDs, asset mapping, and fallback behavior. Do not accept arbitrary URLs or style names from the client.
    
    ## Web admin presentation
    
    - Admin Map: display the avatar inside the rider's map marker and in the associated rider identity detail; keep existing live status, name, and map interactions intact.
    - Inbox: use the avatar in conversation list and selected conversation header, preserving rider name and online/unread indicators.
    - Dispatch: use the avatar in rider assignment choices and tracking identity surfaces where available, preserving availability, selection, and assignment behavior.
    - All locations use the shared ID-to-asset mapping and fall back to initials/person icon for null, missing, or unknown IDs.
    - Set non-decorative image alternatives to rider name; mark decorative duplicates appropriately for assistive technology.
    
    ## Error handling and compatibility
    
    - Migration is safe to re-run and does not rewrite existing user profile data.
    - An invalid avatar ID receives a validation response and never persists.
    - A failed profile update leaves the currently saved avatar in place and communicates the failure without losing the rest of Settings state.
    - Existing login, refresh, rider listing, map, dispatch, and messaging consumers continue to work when `avatar_id` is null or omitted during gradual rollout.
    - Static assets remain available without network access. If an asset fails to render, use the existing initials/person fallback.
    
    ## Security and privacy
    
    - Avatar updates use existing authenticated session and role middleware.
    - The API derives target user ID from the authenticated principal; no client-supplied target ID is accepted for self-service updates.
    - Do not send email, name, or user ID as a DiceBear seed to a third-party runtime API. Static generated assets contain no per-user personal data.
    - Do not expose authentication secrets or include new personal data in logs.
    
    ## Validation
    
    - Server tests: migration behavior, avatar ID allowlist validation, rider-only self-update, cannot update another user, and profile serialization.
    - Mobile tests: settings opens, catalog selection/selected state, save success/failure, offline asset rendering, login welcome only after successful fresh login, correct rider name/avatar, and no welcome on restored session.
    - Web tests: admin Map, Inbox list/detail, and Dispatch assignment render matching assets and fallbacks for null/unknown IDs without changing existing interactions.
    - Run checks for touched packages in repo quality-gate order: lint, typecheck, test, build. Refresh Graphify after code changes.
    
    ## Rollout
    
    1. Add the nullable schema column and backend compatibility fields first.
    2. Bundle the same catalog in mobile and web, and update admin surfaces to handle null values.
    3. Add the mobile avatar selector and persist the profile choice.
    4. Add the fresh-login welcome state.
    5. Verify a selected avatar flows from a rider's profile into all three admin surfaces.
    
    ## Design review notes
    
    - The avatar set contains eight fixed Lorelei Neutral CC0 1.0 renders with distinct deterministic seeds. Preserve the attribution/source notice with the generated asset catalog.
    - The current app login is a single screen with email followed by PIN. The new welcome is a transient post-auth state and must integrate with existing auth redirects without appearing during restored sessions.
    - The existing `ScreenHeader` includes notifications and logout; add Settings without removing or crowding those controls. Preserve accessible target sizing on narrow mobile screens.

    router.post('/', authorize(['admin']), async (req: AuthRequest, res: Response) => {
      try {
        const { name, email, role, department } = req.body || {};
        if (!name || !email || !role) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Missing required account details' });
    
        const tempPassword = crypto.randomBytes(9).toString('base64');
        const hashedPassword = await argon2.hash(tempPassword);
        const id = `${role}_${crypto.randomBytes(4).toString('hex')}`;
        await pool.query('INSERT INTO users (id, email, name, role, department, password_hash, require_password_reset) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)', [id, email, name, role, department || null, hashedPassword, true]);
        res.status(201).json({ success: true, user: { id, name, email, role }, tempPassword });
      } catch (error) {
        res.status(500).json({ error: 'Provisioning failed' });
      }
    });
    
    // Password Reset (Admin only)
    router.post('/:id/reset-password', authorize(['admin']), async (req: AuthRequest, res: Response) => {
      try {
        const { id } = req.params;
        const tempPassword = crypto.randomBytes(12).toString('base64');
        const hashedPassword = await argon2.hash(tempPassword);
        await pool.query('UPDATE users SET password_hash = ?, require_password_reset = ? WHERE id = ?', [hashedPassword, true, id]);
        res.json({ success: true, tempPassword });
      } catch (error) {
        res.status(500).json({ error: 'Reset failed' });
      }
    });
    
    // Delete account (Admin only)
    router.delete('/:id', authorize(['admin']), async (req: AuthRequest, res: Response) => {
      try {
        await pool.query('DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ?', [req.params.id]);
    });

        const { challenge: resetChallenge, newPassword } = req.body || {};

          return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Password reset challenge required' });
        }
    
        const pendingReset = await findAuthChallenge(resetChallenge, 'password_reset');
        if (!pendingReset) return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Invalid or expired password reset challenge' });
        const [rows] = await pool.query(
          'SELECT id, email, role, require_password_reset FROM users WHERE id = ?',
          [pendingReset.userId],

        if (!user || !user.require_password_reset || user.email?.toLowerCase() === 'admin@company.com') {
          return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Invalid or expired password reset challenge' });
        }
    
        const isValidPassword = user.role === 'rider'
          ? /^\d{4}$/.test(newPassword)
          : newPassword.length >= 8 && /\d/.test(newPassword) && /[!@#$%^&*(),.?":{}|<>]/.test(newPassword);
        if (!isValidPassword) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'New password does not meet the account password requirements' });
    
        if (!await consumeAuthChallenge(resetChallenge, 'password_reset')) {
          return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Invalid or expired password reset challenge' });
        }
    
        const hashedPassword = await argon2.hash(newPassword);
    
        const [updateResult] = await pool.query(
          `UPDATE users SET password_hash = ?, require_password_reset = 0, last_password_change = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
             refresh_token = NULL, refresh_token_expires_at = NULL
           WHERE id = ? AND require_password_reset = 1`,
          [hashedPassword, pendingReset.userId],
        ) as any[];
        if (updateResult?.affectedRows !== 1) return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Password reset is no longer required' });
    
        res.json({ success: true, message: 'Password updated successfully' });

        console.error('Update password error:', error);

      }
    });

    const fetchChunkedDrivingRoute = async (points: LatLng[]): Promise<LatLng[]> => {
      const cleanPoints = points.filter(isValidLatLng);
      if (cleanPoints.length < 2) return cleanPoints;
    
      const routed: LatLng[] = [];
    
      for (let start = 0; start < cleanPoints.length - 1; start += MAX_ROUTING_WAYPOINTS - 1) {
        const chunk = cleanPoints.slice(start, start + MAX_ROUTING_WAYPOINTS);
        if (chunk.length < 2) break;
    
        const lngLatChunk = chunk.map(([lat, lng]) => [lng, lat] as LngLat);
        const chunkRoute = await fetchDrivingRoute(lngLatChunk);
        routed.push(...(routed.length > 0 ? chunkRoute.slice(1) : chunkRoute));
      }
    
      return routed.length > 1 ? routed : cleanPoints;
    };

      to: [number, number],
    ) => {
      const [fromLat, fromLng] = from;
      const [toLat, toLng] = to;
    
      const startLat = (fromLat * Math.PI) / 180;
      const startLng = (fromLng * Math.PI) / 180;
      const endLat = (toLat * Math.PI) / 180;
      const endLng = (toLng * Math.PI) / 180;
    
      const y = Math.sin(endLng - startLng) * Math.cos(endLat);
      const x =
        Math.cos(startLat) * Math.sin(endLat) -
        Math.sin(startLat) * Math.cos(endLat) * Math.cos(endLng - startLng);
    
      return ((Math.atan2(y, x) * 180) / Math.PI + 360) % 360;
    };

      const metersPerLat = 111320;
      const metersPerLng = 111320 * Math.cos((atLat * Math.PI) / 180);
      return {
        x: lngDiff * metersPerLng,
        y: latDiff * metersPerLat,
      };

      const vx = endOffset.x - startOffset.x;
      const vy = endOffset.y - startOffset.y;
      const lengthSquared = vx * vx + vy * vy;
      const t = lengthSquared === 0
        ? 0
        : Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (-(startOffset.x * vx + startOffset.y * vy)) / lengthSquared));

          start[1] + (end[1] - start[1]) * t,

        distance: Math.sqrt(
